rule.text: A district appears when the workers in its industries have a location quotient (the city's share of workers in them divided by Canada's share) of at least 1.25 and number at least 1,000 or 1% of the city's workers, or when one of its listed specialities has a location quotient of at least 3 with at least 5,000 workers or 0.5% of the city's workers (and never fewer than 1,000). Districts are ranked by how many workers they have above the national norm (workers minus workers divided by the quotient); up to 5 per city. A Harbor also needs a hex on or next to water or a mapped river. The city type is named after the strongest district, or after a listed district with a quotient of at least 6 and at least 3% of the city's workers when there is one, and labelled by its speciality when one passes; 'Capital city' goes only to Ottawa – Gatineau and 'Seat of government' only to a provincial or territorial capital. These are the U.S. edition's rules, applied to 2021 Census counts of employed residents (table 98-10-0448) in place of jobs counted at employers.
rule.county_note: Census divisions get no districts in the Canadian edition.

catalog.name: Campus
catalog.description: Science and technology: research labs, universities, software publishers, computer services and data hosting.

catalog.name: Commercial hub
catalog.description: Finance and insurance: banks, securities and commodity trading, insurers.

catalog.name: Industrial zone
catalog.description: Manufacturing plus mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction.

catalog.name: Harbor
catalog.description: Water transport: shipping lines, ferries, and port and harbour services.
catalog.caveat: Only for cities with a hex on or next to water or a mapped river.

catalog.name: Theater square
catalog.description: Culture and media: theatres, orchestras, spectator sports, film and music studios, broadcasters.

catalog.name: Entertainment complex
catalog.description: Leisure: amusement parks, casinos, golf, ski and fitness, plus hotels, resorts and camps.

catalog.name: Aerodrome
catalog.description: Aviation: airlines, airport services and aerospace manufacturing.

catalog.name: Government plaza
catalog.description: Federal (except defence) and provincial or territorial public administration. Local and Indigenous governments are in every region and are left out.
catalog.caveat: Public universities, colleges and hospitals are not public administration (they count in Campus).

catalog.name: Encampment
catalog.description: Defence services: members of the Canadian Armed Forces and civilian defence staff.
catalog.caveat: Counted where they live, and only those in private households (the census long form leaves out barracks).

catalog.name: Aqueduct & dam
catalog.description: Utilities: electric power generation and distribution, water, sewage and gas.
